summary: Songeun Choe works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by Myung-dae Moon for an MA, Choe completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonja Arntzen is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1967–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz (~1972–1979), and also studied under Seizan Yanagida (~1973–1974) and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. She completed her Magisterexamen, Promotion, and Habilitation at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1986–2005), where she was later Akademische Oberrätin (2007), holding posts at Vienna (2008) and Munich (2009–2010).

Sonya S. Lee works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Wu Hung (attested 2004), taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004), and joined the University of Southern California (attested 2010).

Soonil Hwang specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. After completing an MA under Seung-won Seo at Dongguk University, Hwang earned a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, later holding a post at Dongguk University.

Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858. He held a post at Uppsala University and was appointed professor of comparative philology, comparative Indo-European linguistics, and Old Norse at the University of Oslo in 1866.

Soshuku Shibatani is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Educated at Waseda University and Koyasan University (MA 2003–2007, PhD 2013), Shibatani held roles at Sonoda Women's University, Junrei Henro Kenkyukai (2014), and Koyasan University (attested 2015).
Soshū Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at International Buddhist University (attested in 2000 and 2015).

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Fusho Nagano, Bokusan Nishiari, and Teizo Shiratori. He served as professor/dean (1899) and president (1918) at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Sras Rinpoche III is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric Monastery. He served as abbot at Drepung Loseling (1984), held leadership at Gyume (1995–2008), and served at Rizong Monastery.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology, holding degrees from the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016). She held teaching posts at Rice, UNC Wilmington, Montana, and Houston (~2022), and a fellowship at Harvard (~2020–2023).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966), and served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1977–1997).

Sri Anirvan was an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his education in India, studying at Sanskrit College and University (~1912–1916), the University of Calcutta (~1916–1918), and the University of Dhaka.

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg (~1962–1967). He subsequently served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

Srisa Chandra Vasu was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Rang Mahal School and Government College University, Lahore (BA ~1877–1881). He served as Vakil at Allahabad High Court (1891), founded Panini Office (1891), and was a Fellow at Allahabad University.

Stacey Van Vleet works in Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. She earned an MA at the University of Colorado and a PhD at Columbia University (attested 2006), where she also held an academic post (attested 2013).

Stamford Raffles was an English administrator and historical and linguistic researcher. He worked for the East India Company (~1795–1824), founded the Zoological Society of London in 1825, and served as its president in 1826.

Stanislas Julien was a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat at the Collège de France, where he served as Chair of Chinese (1832–1873), later also teaching at INALCO (1863–1871).

Stanislav Grof is a psychiatrist and researcher in religious studies and other fields who studied at Charles University (~1951–1956). His career included posts at Johns Hopkins, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Esalen Institute, and the California Institute of Integral Studies.

Stanisław Schayer was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He became a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society (~1933–1941) and the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences (~1935–1941).
